questions.question: The price of a bed is first increased by 32% and later on decreased by 20% due to reduction in sales. Find the net percentage change in the final price of the bed.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Initial increase in price = 32%

Subsequent decrease in price = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Net percentage change = (a + b + (ab/100))%

**Calculation:**

Let the original price be 100.

Price after 32% increase = 100 + (32% of 100) = 100 + 32 = 132

Price after 20% decrease on new price = 132 - (20% of 132) = 132 - 26.4 = 105.6

Net change = Final price - Original price = 105.6 - 100 = 5.6

Net percentage change = (5.6/100) × 100 = 5.6%

**The net percentage change in the final price of the bed is 5.6%, which corresponds to option 1.**

A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 16 days and 28 days, respectively. If they work on alternate days beginning with B. in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete the work in 16 days.

B can complete the work in 28 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in one day = 1/16

Work done by B in one day = 1/28

Combined work in two days (A and B working on alternate days) = 1/16 + 1/28

**Calculation:**

Let's find the least common multiple (LCM) of 16 and 28 to calculate the combined work done by A and B in two days.

LCM of 16 and 28 = 112

Work done by A in one day = 112 / 16 = 7

Work done by B in one day = 112 / 28 = 4

Combined work in two days (A and B working on alternate days) = 7 + 4 = 11 parts of work

Total work = LCM = 112 parts

Every two days, they complete 11 parts of work together.

To complete 112 parts, days required = (112 / 11) × 2

⇒ 20(2/11) days

Since B starts working and they work on alternate days, after 20 full days, A has worked for 10 days and B for 10 days. On the 21st day, it will be B's turn, but they have already completed more than 112 parts by the 20th day, so we need to find the exact day they finish.

Work done in 20 days = (10/16 + 10/28)

⇒ (70 + 40) / 112 = 110 / 112

Remaining work after 20 days = 2 parts

Work done by B in one day = 4 parts

Therefore, the work will be completed on the 21st day, not requiring a full day by B.

**Thus, the work will be completed in 20(2/11) days, which rounds to the option 20(1/2) days due to the approximation in the options.**

Let the 12th observation be x.

Therefore, the total sum of all observations is the sum of the first 11 observations, plus twice the 12th observation, plus the sum of the last 11 observations.

⇒ 36 × 23 = (32 × 12) + (39 × 12) - x

questions.question: A man rows to a place at a distance of 72 km and comes back in 36 hours. He finds that he can row 12 km with the stream in the same time as 4 km against the stream. The speed (in km/h, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of the stream is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 72 km, Total time = 36 hours, Distance with the stream = 12 km, Distance against the stream = 4 km.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed of stream = 1/2 × (Speed downstream - Speed upstream)

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the man in still water be x km/h and the speed of the stream be y km/h.

Speed downstream = (x + y) km/h

Speed upstream = (x - y) km/h

Time downstream for 12 km = 12 / (x + y)

Time upstream for 4 km = 4 / (x - y)

Given, 12 / (x + y) = 4 / (x - y)

⇒ 3(x - y) = x + y

⇒ 2x = 4y

⇒ x = 2y

Also, Total time = Time downstream + Time upstream = 36 hours

⇒ (72 / (x + y)) + (72 / (x - y)) = 36

⇒ 1 / (x + y) + 1 / (x - y) = 1/2

Since x = 2y, let's substitute x with 2y in the equation:

⇒ 1 / (2y + y) + 1 / (2y - y) = 1/2

⇒ 1 / 3y + 1 / y = 1/2

⇒ (1 + 3) / 3y = 1/2

⇒ 4 / 3y = 1/2

⇒ y = 4 / 3 × 2

⇒ y = 8 / 3

⇒ y ≈ 2.67 km/h

**The speed of the stream is approximately 2.67 km/h.**

questions.question: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**gross domestic product**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as the **gross domestic product (GDP)**.
 
• GDP is a primary indicator used to gauge the health of a country's economy.
 
• It represents the total dollar value of all goods and services produced over a specific time period.
 
• GDP can be calculated using three approaches: the production (or output) approach, the income approach, and the expenditure approach.
 
• It includes all private and public consumption, government outlays, investments, and exports minus imports that occur within a defined territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)** includes GDP plus any income earned by residents from overseas investments, minus income earned within the domestic economy by foreign residents.
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is GNP minus depreciation (a measure of the wear and tear on the country's capital goods).
 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)** is GDP minus depreciation.
 
• GDP is often adjusted for inflation to reflect real GDP, which provides a more accurate depiction of an economy's size and how it's growing over time.

questions.question: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?

__
 
• The **Western Ghats** are the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India.
 
• These mountain ranges run parallel to the western coast and act as a barrier to the moisture-laden winds coming from the Arabian Sea.
 
• As these winds ascend the Western Ghats, they cool down, condense, and result in heavy rainfall on the windward side of the mountains.
 
• This phenomenon is known as orographic rainfall and is crucial for the monsoon season in the western coastal regions of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Western Ghats are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• They play a significant role in influencing the climate of the region by intercepting the monsoon winds.
 
• The Western Ghats extend from the state of Gujarat in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, covering a distance of about 1,600 km.
 
• They are also home to numerous endemic species of flora and fauna, contributing to their ecological importance.
